overall_summary: Bitcoin sits under 80k with liquidations and Fed jitters setting a cautious tone as traders wait on Wednesday's rate decision. Fresh spot ETF inflows and Franklin Templeton's new dividend-to-Bitcoin products offer institutional support, while easier yields help offset a firm dollar. Geopolitical headlines remain noisy but secondary for crypto direction right now.
key_points: BTC under 80k on liquidations and Fed jitters
Fed expected to hold rates this Wednesday
Yields ease near 5 percent; dollar stays firm

items.title: Bitcoin Slips Under $80K Amid Liquidations and Fed Jitters
items.summary: Bitcoin fell below the eighty thousand dollar level over the weekend, briefly touching near seventy-nine thousand one hundred as hundreds of millions in leveraged long positions were liquidated. High oil prices, AI-related equity weakness, and positioning ahead of Wednesday's Federal Reserve decision added to the pressure, with traders de-risking into the event. This tests a major psychological support and sets up potential volatility as macro data and the rate decision hit this week.
items.impact: Elevated short-term volatility around key support

items.title: Spot Bitcoin ETFs Break Outflow Streak With $301M Inflows
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded roughly three hundred one million dollars in net inflows for the week, snapping a two-week streak of outflows. Strong buying early in the week brought in over one billion, but Thursday and Friday saw about seven hundred seventy-four million exit as prices retreated toward eighty thousand. This shows institutional demand is still present but often reactive to price drops rather than buying dips aggressively.
items.impact: Mixed signal on institutional bid strength

items.title: Galaxy Finds 55% of Bitcoin Supply Unlinked to Known Holders
items.summary: Galaxy Research estimates about eleven point one million Bitcoin, or fifty-five percent of the mined supply, cannot be attributed to known entities such as exchanges, ETFs, governments or identified institutions. Head of research Alex Thorn noted this points to substantial self-custody by individuals, though lost coins and unidentified wallets also play a role. Traders should care because it underscores the true free float and long-term holder base beyond visible institutional piles.
items.impact: Supports narrative of resilient self-custody distribution

items.title: Franklin Templeton Finalizes Dividend-to-Bitcoin ETFs
items.summary: Franklin Templeton completed key SEC filings for two ETFs that hold US large-cap or innovation stocks and automatically reinvest all dividends into Bitcoin, starting with a ninety-five percent equity and five percent Bitcoin mix. The products, with tickers including FBEQ, carry low fees and an effective date around October twenty-seven for potential Nasdaq listing. This opens a passive, rules-based channel for traditional equity investors to build Bitcoin exposure without active crypto decisions.
items.impact: New structural demand pathway from equity portfolios

items.title: Short-Term Holders' Profit Cushion Narrows to 5.9% at $76K
items.summary: On-chain data shows Bitcoin held less than six months now carries an average cost basis near seventy-six thousand dollars, leaving short-term holders with only a five point nine percent unrealized profit margin after recent price weakness. That cushion has tightened from higher levels last week as costs rose and price slipped. A break below this level would put a large recent buyer cohort underwater and could increase selling pressure if it triggers stop-outs or capitulation.
items.impact: Key support level to watch for potential cascade risk

items.title: CoinDCX Absorbs $16M USDT Loss From Old Wallets
items.summary: Indian exchange CoinDCX confirmed a loss of roughly fifteen point nine nine million USDT from deprecated deposit wallets tied to a prior 2025 incident, after first dismissing reports as a false alarm. The firm said a failed sweeping system left deposits exposed and it is absorbing the full amount so customer funds remain unaffected. Exchange operational failures like this can weigh on broader market confidence even when users are made whole.
items.impact: Minor hit to exchange trust and stablecoin flow optics

items.title: Fed Set to Hold Rates Wednesday After September Hike
items.summary: The Federal Reserve is widely expected to keep the funds rate at 3.75 to 4.00 percent when it decides on Wednesday, following the first hike since 2023 in September. Markets price roughly 90 percent odds of a pause, with attention on Chair Kevin Warsh's language and any signal that December remains live given sticky inflation near 3.7 percent. Crypto and risk assets traders should care because the statement and press conference will set near-term rate path expectations and volatility into year-end.
items.impact: Likely muted immediate move if hold confirmed; guidance drives next leg for yields and BTC

items.title: 10-Year Yields Ease Near 5 Percent Ahead of FOMC
items.summary: US 10-year Treasury yields have pulled back toward the 4.97 to 5.00 percent area in recent sessions after briefly higher levels, with two-year yields also softer as markets lock in an October hold. Safe-haven flows and oil volatility have supported bonds. For traders this matters because lower yields ease financial conditions and often support Bitcoin and equities, while still-elevated levels keep the higher-for-longer narrative intact heading into GDP and PCE data.
items.impact: Softer yields supportive for risk assets including crypto if sustained

items.title: Dollar Index Holds Firm Near 102 on Rate Outlook
items.summary: The DXY is trading around 101.7 to 102, little changed to slightly softer early Monday but supported by firm yields and expectations of resilient US growth requiring potential further Fed tightening later. It remains near recent highs. Crypto traders watch the dollar closely because a strong greenback typically pressures Bitcoin and other risk assets via tighter global liquidity conditions.
items.impact: Firm DXY headwind for BTC and commodities if it holds or rises

items.title: Oil Retreats from Multi-Month Highs on De-Escalation Hopes
items.summary: Crude prices fell Monday, with WTI near 101 dollars and Brent around 115, after last week's surge toward multi-month highs driven by Middle East tensions and Iran-related risks. Hopes of easing hostilities via mediators provided relief, though risks remain elevated post-midterms. Traders should care because lower oil eases inflation pressure and Fed hawkishness, while still-high prices keep sticky PCE risks alive for Thursday's data.
items.impact: Eases near-term inflation fears, potentially supportive for risk assets

items.title: Strong Q3 GDP and Sticky PCE Eyed for Thursday
items.summary: Advance Q3 GDP is forecast around 3.0 to 3.2 percent annualized, accelerating from 2.2 percent prior, with Atlanta Fed tracking near 3.5 percent, while September core PCE is seen at about 3.1 percent year-over-year. These land the morning after the Fed decision. This double release will test whether growth and inflation justify more hikes, directly shaping December odds and market pricing for crypto into year-end.
items.impact: Hot prints keep December hike live and volatility elevated

items.title: Monday Data: Chicago Fed Activity and Dallas Manufacturing
items.summary: Today brings the Chicago Fed National Activity Index for September, expected near minus 0.1, and the Dallas Fed Manufacturing Index for October, seen around 7 from prior 9.8, plus Treasury bill and two-year note auctions. These are secondary but give a pulse on activity and regional factory conditions right before the FOMC blackout ends. Light impact expected unless big surprises, but they fill the data void ahead of the heavy midweek calendar for macro-sensitive crypto trading.
items.impact: Limited market mover unless outlier readings shift Fed pricing

items.title: Trump Rules Out Iran Strike Today, Weighs Deal or Finish-Off
items.summary: President Trump said there will be no U.S. strike on Iran on Sunday, but he is still deciding whether to make a deal or finish the job after months of war. Qatari mediators visited Tehran while U.S. and Israeli planners keep post-midterm strike options ready. Traders should watch this closely because any renewed attack or breakthrough deal would swing oil prices hard and drive broad risk-on or risk-off moves across crypto and equities.
items.impact: Unresolved binary catalyst for oil and risk assets ahead of U.S. midterms

items.title: Houthis Target Riyadh Again as Oil Holds Near Multi-Month Highs
items.summary: Saudi-led forces intercepted another Houthi ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh as the capital’s airport tried to resume flights after deadly earlier strikes. Iran-backed rebels also claimed hits on oil facilities while tanker attacks and mine risks persist near the Strait of Hormuz. Elevated Brent near one hundred ten to one hundred fifteen dollars keeps inflation pressure high and supports a risk-off tone that crypto traders cannot ignore.
items.impact: Sustained energy supply premium and inflation drag on risk assets

items.title: Lula Wins Historic Fourth Term; Bolsonaro Rejects Result
items.summary: Brazil’s Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva staged a rare comeback to win the presidential runoff with about fifty-two percent against Flávio Bolsonaro. The defeated candidate refused to concede and called for the vote to be annulled, echoing his father’s contested 2022 loss. Markets that had priced a right-wing win now face political uncertainty in a major commodity exporter, which can spill into emerging-market risk appetite and global growth bets.
items.impact: EM political risk and Brazil asset volatility with limited direct crypto catalyst

items.title: Serbia’s Vučić Concedes Defeat to Student Protest Movement
items.summary: Longtime Serbian leader Aleksandar Vučić conceded snap parliamentary elections to the Student List after nearly two years of anti-corruption protests. The opposition is projected to take a clear majority in the two-hundred-fifty-seat assembly, ending more than a decade of his party’s dominance. The shift weakens a key pro-Russia voice in the Balkans and adds to Europe’s political realignment, though immediate market impact is secondary to larger oil and Iran risks.
items.impact: European political realignment with modest regional risk premium

items.title: Ukraine Starlink Speeds Fully Restored After Musk Throttle
items.summary: Kyiv confirmed Starlink and Starshield returned to full pre-restriction speeds after more than a week of slowdowns that hurt drone and logistics operations. Elon Musk said Ukraine violated terms by using the service for offensive strikes, while Zelenskyy thanked U.S. partners including Trump for helping reverse it. Restored battlefield connectivity reduces near-term military disruption for Ukraine but highlights private-sector leverage over a major war, a watch item for geopolitical risk pricing.
items.impact: Stabilizes Ukraine military ops; limited broad market move

items.title: Israel Votes Tomorrow in Tight Race Over Netanyahu’s Future
items.summary: Israelis head to the polls on October twenty-seventh in the first national election since the October seventh attacks, widely seen as a referendum on Benjamin Netanyahu. Polls show his bloc and the opposition led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot neck-and-neck, with neither side clearly able to reach sixty-one seats. The outcome will shape Israel’s Iran strategy, Gaza policy, and U.S. coordination just as Trump weighs further Middle East military moves, keeping a major geopolitical wildcard on the calendar.
items.impact: Near-term event risk for Middle East policy and oil premium
